verdicts.note: Economic impact of multiple sclerosis on families.
Commentary on the agenda of population studies.
No abstract. CHILDREN's living arrangements in developing countries is a different construct from a young adult's, but the title alone cannot settle it.

Patrilocality and early marital co-residence in rural China 1955-85, testing modernisation against tradition-restored and demographic-determinism accounts. Exposure trend for the extended arm's largest setting, no fertility outcome.
Women's status, fertility and contraception in a Maharashtra village; the arrangement is not the exposure.
Adolescents' beliefs about the life course.
Co-residence as the dominant support pattern for the Korean elderly. The homonym.
Fertility decline and the familial support system for the Thai elderly; runs from fertility to elderly co-residence.
Contraction stage of the Chinese family life cycle; children's departure is an accounting stage.
Transitions in the living arrangements of elderly nonmarried parents. The homonym, with the arrangement as outcome.
Australian population trends; household formation is one reported series.
Dutch cohort trends in age at leaving the parental home reported alongside fertility, and notes the 1988 share living with parents EXCEEDED 1982. Descriptive on both links, estimating neither.
Predictors of home leaving and repeated home leaving among American youth, NSFH, event history. Link 1; the repeat-leaving focus is useful for measurement in §9.
Twenty-year restudy of a Malay village; population and household change described.

Cigno-model determinants of completed and intended fertility in Japan with co-residence with the parents among the regressors. Whether co-residence is the exposure or one covariate among many is not settled by the abstract; full-text read.
Commentary on development aid and birth limitation. 'Boomerang' here is the metaphor, not the return home.
Spousal fertility discussion as an intermediate factor in Guangdong.
Household forms and living standards in preindustrial France; family size and household form over the life course. Pre-modern, A.7's under Ruling 2.
No abstract; fetal and child mortality among the Hmong is decisive on subject.

Event-history analysis of the first-birth interval in Nepal with POSTMARITAL LIVING ARRANGEMENTS as the exposure, finding extended-household residence with reduced natal-kin contact matters and naming coital frequency as the mechanism. A direct arrangement-to-birth estimate, and it names the A.14 channel.

Long first-birth intervals in North India after early marriage, with standard explanations rejected. Post-marital residence with in-laws is the usual candidate but the abstract does not say; full-text read.
Culture and class as determinants of out-of-wedlock childbearing.
Prevalence of one-person households in Korea.

Family instability and premarital birth using NSFH parental fertility, marital AND home-leaving histories. Home-leaving is a covariate in a fertility model rather than the exposure, but the data structure is the one this chapter wants; full-text read.

The SEQUENCING of nest-leaving, marriage and first birth among young women -- which is §3's joint-determination problem taken as the object of study rather than as a nuisance. Priority read for the pre-launch arm.

Policy-oriented analysis of Japanese family size with LIVING IN THE PARENTAL HOME among the exposures, alongside income, wife's employment and home ownership. A pre-launch arrangement-to-fertility estimate, and it carries the C.2.c boundary variables in the same model.
Value of sons and old-age security in patrilocal kinship systems. C.3.c's.
Living arrangements of never-married mothers in Botswana, Namibia and Zambia, most remaining in the parental home. Childbearing determines the arrangement here, not the reverse.
Covariates of household extension in rural India over time; the arrangement is the outcome.
Parent-child relations and offspring psychological wellbeing.
Children at home and women's wellbeing by employment status.
No abstract; 'Thai elderly who do not coreside with their children' is decisive on the homonym.
Book review of a Peruvian macroeconomic volume.

Housework time across six living situations INCLUDING never-married living with parents versus never-married living independently. Exactly the pre-launch contrast, with housework rather than fertility as the outcome.
No abstract; foster-care youth preparation is decisive on subject.

GRANDPARENTAL CO-RESIDENCE with adolescent women against early childbearing, finding co-residence DELAYS first birth beyond the teenage years. A pre-launch arrangement-to-birth estimate with A.23's predicted negative sign, in a configuration the scope did not enumerate -- three generations with the young woman as the pre-launch member.
Race differences in family structure 1880-1980; children residing without parents is the outcome.
Household arrangements OF adolescent mothers -- nuclear versus extended. Childbearing precedes and shapes the arrangement.
Parenting quality in multigenerational African-American families; the arrangement is the setting and the outcome is mothering behaviour.
Dutch FFS typology of home leavers by age at leaving; link 1.

Dutch FFS description of the sequence from leaving home through living alone, cohabitation, marriage and first motherhood, and the ages at which each occurs. Descriptive but it is the whole chain in one dataset.
Population profile of Tibet.
Life-table simulation in which declining fertility and changing nuptiality drive elderly co-residence in Taiwan. Homonym and reverse arrow together.
Polish women's careers against reproductive behaviour by family life-cycle stage.
Urban family structure in late antiquity from Chrysostom; the co-residing group is defined, not estimated.
Chinese household size and structure as consequences of population policy and fertility decline.

Patrilocality against childbearing AND the labour supply and earnings of married Japanese women, in one analysis. Directly on the extended arm, and it carries both the fertility outcome and the labour-supply outcome the scope named as the largest route-out -- so it can show whether they are separable.
Child prostitution.
Racial differences in intergenerational co-residence among people aged 74+. The homonym.
Parenthood status and oncology treatment preferences.
Unmarried adult children's exchange with parents; support flows, not fertility.
No abstract; elderly poverty alleviation through living with family is decisive on the homonym.
Maternal parenting practices; children living at home is a covariate.
Hmong demographic and ecological change in Laos.
Household formation and inheritance patterns as determinants of women's autonomy, contrasting preindustrial northern Europe with contemporary northern India. Theory for the §6 configuration split.
